text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Allegations of nepotism and maladministration have been levelled at the Food Management and Logistics Unit of the Council of Churches of Namibia, which is responsible for the distribution of drought relief aid in the country.

- The monthly Crop Assessment Report says record national production of 154,300 tonnes of cereals is forecast for this year, following good rains experienced countrywide. Last year's production was 82,700 tonnes.

- Namibia, South Africa and Angola have launched a joint venture research project, partnered by Germany, Norway, Russia and Britain, aimed at gathering detailed information about the marine environment in the Benguela current and the dynamics of fish stocks there.
- Namibian police public relations chief Hophni Hamufungu is to appear in court to face charges of drunken driving.
- Nine people died in a head-on collision between a minibus and an Angola truck in northern Namibia.
